arxiv-2011-11221.title: Adversarial Refinement Network for Human Motion Prediction
arxiv-2011-11221.creator: Xianjin CHAO, Yanrui Bin, Wenqing Chu, Xuan Cao, Yanhao Ge, Chengjie Wang, Jilin Li, Feiyue Huang, Howard Leung
arxiv-2011-11221.description: Abstract Human motion prediction aims to predict future 3D skeletal sequences by giving a limited human motion as inputs. Two popular methods, recurrent neural networks and feed-forward deep networks, are able to predict rough motion trend, but motion details such as limb movement may be lost.

arxiv-2012-09788.title: Neutrino Energy Estimation in Neutral Current Interactions and Prospects for Sterile Neutrino Searches
arxiv-2012-09788.creator: A. P. Furmanski, C. Hilgenberg
arxiv-2012-09788.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by A. P. Furmanski, C. Hilgenberg. Modern neutrino detectors, particularly the large liquid argon time projection chambers (LAr TPCs) at SBN and DUNE, provide an unprecedented amount of information about GeV-scale interactions. By taking advantage of the excellent spatial and calorimetric resolution as well as the low tracking thresholds provided by LAr TPCs, we present a novel method of estimating the neutrino energy in neutral current interactions.

arxiv-2208-06805.title: Shadows around Sgr A* and M87* as a tool to test gravity theories
arxiv-2208-06805.creator: Alexander F. Zakharov
arxiv-2208-06805.description: Abstract In the framework of Randall – Sundrum theory with extra dimension Reissner – Nordström black hole solutions with a tidal charge have been found. The shadow around the supermassive black hole in M87 was reconstructed in 2019 based on observations with the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) in April 2017.

arxiv-2212-04352.title: Correlated quantum dynamics of graphene
arxiv-2212-04352.creator: François Rousse, Olle Eriksson, Magnus Ögren
arxiv-2212-04352.description: Abstract Phase-space representations are a family of methods for dynamics of both bosonic and fermionic systems, that work by mapping the system’s density matrix to a quasi-probability density and the Liouville-von Neumann equation of the Hamiltonian to a corresponding density differential equation for the probability.

arxiv-2306-06194.title: Share, Collaborate, Benchmark: Advancing Travel Demand Research through rigorous open-source collaboration.
arxiv-2306-06194.creator: Juan D. Caicedo, Carlos Guirado, Marta C. González, Joan L. Walker
arxiv-2306-06194.description: Abstract This research foregrounds general practices in travel demand research, emphasizing the need to change our ways. A critical barrier preventing travel demand literature from effectively informing policy is the volume of publications without clear, consolidated benchmarks, making it difficult for researchers and policymakers to gather insights and use models to guide decision-making.

arxiv-2410-24008.title: On the Chern filtration for the moduli of bundles on curves
arxiv-2410-24008.creator: Woonam Lim, Miguel Moreira, Weite Pi
arxiv-2410-24008.description: Abstract . We introduce and study the Chern filtration on the cohomology of the moduli of bundles on curves. This can be viewed as a natural cohomological invariant defined via tautological classes that interpolates between additive Betti numbers and the multiplicative ring structure.

arxiv-2505-08698.title: Continuous Temporal Learning of Probability Distributions via Neural ODEs with Applications in Continuous Glucose Monitoring Data
arxiv-2505-08698.creator: Antonio Álvarez-López, Marcos Matabuena
arxiv-2505-08698.description: Abstract Modeling the dynamics of probability distributions from time-dependent data samples is a fundamental problem in many fields, including digital health. The goal is to analyze how the distribution of a biomarker, such as glucose, changes over time and how these changes may reflect the progression of chronic diseases such as diabetes.

pmc-11669454.creator: Poppy MacInnes, Marilia A. Calcia, Michela Martinuzzi, Cora Griffin, Siân Oram, Louise M. Howard
pmc-11669454.description: Aims and methodWe used data from Domestic Homicide Reviews (DHRs) to describe the patterns of mental health service use by perpetrators of domestic homicide in England and Wales. In 186 DHR reports we compared the characteristics of perpetrators who accessed mental health services with those of perpetrators who did not.

pmc-11676717.title: A Spectroscopy Solution for Contactless Conductivity Detection in Capillary Electrophoresis
pmc-11676717.creator: Tomas Drevinskas, Audrius Maruška, Hirotaka Ihara, Makoto Takafuji, Linas Jonušauskas, Domantas Armonavičius, Mantas Stankevičius, Kristina Bimbiraitė-Survilienė, Elzbieta Skrzydlewska, Ona Ragažinskienė, Yutaka Kuwahara, Shoji Nagaoka, Vilma Kaškonienė, Loreta Kubilienė
pmc-11676717.description: This paper introduces a novel contactless single-chip detector that utilizes impedance-to-digital conversion technology to measure impedance in the microfluidic channel or capillary format analytical device. The detector is designed to operate similarly to capacitively coupled contactless conductivity detectors for capillary electrophoresis or chromatography but with the added capability of performing frequency sweeps up to 200 kHz.

pmc-12686821.title: Model-guided chemical environment and metabolic network design to couple pathways with cell fitness
pmc-12686821.creator: Natalia Kakko von Koch, Tuula Tenkanen, Sandra Castillo, Virve Vidgren, Tino Koponen, Kristoffer Krogerus, Merja Penttilä, Paula Jouhten
pmc-12686821.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Heterologous compound production is a complex trait since the native metabolic fluxes supplying the precursors, redox power, and energy are under multilevel cellular regulation. Improving complex traits using targeted engineering needs combinatorially charting the complex genetic underpinnings. While this is laborious, adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) has been used to improve many traits of microbial strains that are of application relevance such as tolerance of harsh conditions and nutrient utilization.

pmc-12737361.title: Study of the Activity of the Staphylococcus aureus Phage vB_SaS_GE1 Against MRSA Clinical Isolates and Its Impact on the Formation of Dual-Species Biofilms with P. aeruginosa

pmc-12737361.description: Bacteriophage therapy is regarded as a promising alternative for treating and preventing antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections. Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is one of the most prevalent and difficult-to-treat pathogens. S. aureus also contributes to the formation of both single- and mixed-species biofilms.

pmc-12796250.title: Constructing flexible sub-nanometer ferroelectric catalyst to overcome heterocatalytic kinetic barriers for enhanced catalytic and immuno-therapy
pmc-12796250.creator: Rui Zhang, Yuanfei Yao, Lu Yang, Xudong Zhao, Boshi Tian, Dan Yang, Piaoping Yang
pmc-12796250.description: Piezoelectric catalysis enhances therapeutic outcomes in nanocatalysis but is limited by intrinsic catalysis mechanism. This study employs sub-nanometer Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) nanowires as a piezoelectric catalyst to address these challenges. Oxygen K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy and spherical aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy reveal the orthorhombic phase (Pca21) in HZO nanowires. This structure imparts polymer-like flexibility to Hf0.5Zr0.

pmc-12848043.title: High temperature evaporative cooler utilizing boiling suppression at water’s boiling point
pmc-12848043.creator: Ranran Fang, Zeyu Sun, Quan Chen, Jiangen Zheng, Zhonghua Yan, Nana Pan, Yi Li, Yongyi Deng, Yongbin Wei, Zhu Liang, Anatoliy Y Vorobyev
pmc-12848043.description: We experimentally demonstrate boiling suppression in a water film confined within superhydrophilic hierarchical nano/microstructured surfaces, enabling intense interfacial steam generation without bubble formation at the boiling point. Leveraging this phenomenon, we develop a high-temperature dew point evaporative cooler capable of reducing hot airflow from 437 °C to below ambient temperature.

pmc-13063526.title: Interfragmentary compression in a feline sacroiliac luxation model: biomechanical comparison of cannulated compression headless screws and cortical screws applied in positional or lag fashion
pmc-13063526.creator: Laura Wachsmuth, Josef Wieser, Christoph Thorwächter, Yury Zablotski, Nina Dorothee Lorenz, Susanne Lauer, Matthias Kornmayer
pmc-13063526.description: BackgroundThe purpose of this study was to compare the efficacy of cannulated compression headless screws (CCHS) with cortical positional and lag screws in generating interfragmentary compression in a simulated feline sacroiliac luxation fracture (SILF) model. In this ex vivo biomechanical study thirty-six cadavers of adult domestic short-haired cats with simulated unilateral SILF were allocated to three groups.

pmc-13374703.creator: Eleni Galanis, Nicholas H Ogden
pmc-13374703.description: tiques dans de nouvelles régions du Canada. pmc-13500719.title: Fluorine-free acetonitrile-based electrolytes with anion-reinforced solvation chemistry for sustainable sodium-ion full batteries
pmc-13500719.creator: Xu Xu, Jian Chen, Zhuo Yang, Zhiming Zhou, Xiaosa Zhang, Xinhui Zeng, Yun Wan, Xiaomin Chen, Wenxi Kuang, Xiaoyan Shi, Lingling Zhang, Xunzhu Zhou, Shulei Chou, Lin Li
pmc-13500719.description: Acetonitrile-based electrolytes have garnered significant attention for sodium-ion batteries due to their high ionic conductivity and favorable oxidation resistance. However, their practical implementation is hindered by an unsatisfactory anti-reduction ability, leading to poor compatibility with hard carbon anode and, consequently, rapid capacity degradation.

pmc-13505433.title: Pediatric septorhinoplasty: A cohort study utilizing the pediatric health information system (PHIS) database☆
pmc-13505433.creator: Molly F MacIsaac, Ryan D Hoffman, Joshua M Wright, Jordan N Halsey, S Alex Rottgers
pmc-13505433.description: BackgroundPediatric rhinoplasty and septoplasty are performed for both functional and reconstructive indications, including airway obstruction, trauma, and orofacial cleft (OFC)-associated nasal deformities. Despite increasing national case volume, limited data exist on utilization patterns, procedural trends, and healthcare costs in this population.

pmc-13588265.title: Epigenome-wide association analysis of prenatal organophosphate ester flame retardant exposure in maternal blood implicates maternal immune and neuronal epigenetic alterations
pmc-13588265.creator: Wanyi Tang, Helen Foley, Xiaoran Yang, Sahra Mohazzab-Hosseinian, Tingyu Yang, Ixel Hernandez-Castro, Kurunthachalam Kannan, Yijin Xiang, Huaiyu Mi, Joseph Wiemels, Juan Pablo Lewinger, Kimberly Siegmund, Theresa Bastain, Carrie Breton, Chang Shu
pmc-13588265.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background:Organophosphate esters (OPEs) are widely used flame retardants and plasticizers prevalent in indoor air, dust, and water. Studies suggest prenatal OPE exposure is linked to adverse maternal and infant outcomes, but the biological mechanisms remain unclear.Methods:We examined associations between nine urinary OPE metabolites measured in the third trimester and DNA methylation in maternal blood from 175 pregnant women in the MADRES cohort. 837,856 CpGs were profiled using the Illumina EPIC array.
